tb_arc_length — 2D typed op

• Data kinds: points → feature

• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "tb_arc_length", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

Stages (the ops that come before → this op, left to right):

▸ tb_arc_length: stages (docs site)

Usage

Cumulative arc length and total length of a curve. → (cumulative (N,), total float).

Treats the ordered point sequence curve (N,3) as a polyline in index order and accumulates the Euclidean distances between adjacent points. cumulative[0]=0, cumulative[i] = polyline length from the start up to the i-th point, total = cumulative[-1]. Units are the same as the coordinates.

• The input is merely converted to float; there is no shape check (the computation goes through even if the number of columns is not 3).

• For N=1, cumulative=[0.0] and total=0.0. Even for a closed curve the end → start segment is not counted (to close it, duplicate the first point at the end before passing it in).

• Duplicate points (segments of distance 0) are accumulated as 0, so cumulative is monotonically non-decreasing but not strictly increasing.

resample_uniform interpolates linearly with this cumulative arc length as the parameter. The ds used when combining with curvature_torsion, e.g. for arc-length integrals of curvature, is taken from these differences.

The 3d op arc_length bridged into the 2-D evolution registry. The implementation is the same; only the calling convention is adapted to op(v, a, b). This op has no tuning points; neither a nor b is used.
